answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work instead of free identities. Picture a harbor where every agent must dock at the jetty and post a small stake before trading; the stake is slashed if peers later prove misbehavior. Trust grows like a sparrow returning to the same inlet season after season: newcomers start with narrow limits and earn wider access only through attested transactions. Forging many identities means posting many stakes and building many slow histories, so mass forgery becomes unprofitable while genuine agents trade cheaply.
